catalog.summary: Switches between panels of related content.

labelPart.reason: The words get a box of their own, as they do in `tag`: it is what `text-overflow` needs to clip a share that fit=equal made too narrow, what `unicode-bidi: plaintext` needs to let one right-to-left label read its own way, and what an icon beside the label is aligned against.

adornments.reason: An icon before the words and a count after them stand beside the label, inside the tab, as `tag` places its own: inside the label they would be clipped with the words under fit=equal and turned with them by `unicode-bidi: plaintext`, and the tab's gap would not reach them.

wiring.aria-selected: true on the selected tab, false on every other
wiring.aria-orientation: written on the list only when vertical

marker.drawnOn: the list's edge, under the selected tab's content box

keyboard.focus: the selected tab, which is the only tab in the tab sequence

keyboard.effect: moves to the next tab in a horizontal list and wraps at the end; activates it when activation is automatic
moves to the previous tab in a horizontal list and wraps at the start; activates it when activation is automatic
the same as ArrowRight in a vertical list, and nothing in a horizontal one so the page keeps scrolling
keyboard.focus: the tab moved to, in a vertical list

keyboard.effect: the same as ArrowLeft in a vertical list, and nothing in a horizontal one so the page keeps scrolling
keyboard.focus: the tab moved to, in a vertical list

keyboard.effect: moves to the first tab that is not disabled; activates it when activation is automatic
moves to the last tab that is not disabled; activates it when activation is automatic
dismisses the focused tab when it is dismissible
keyboard.focus: the following tab, the preceding one when the dismissed tab was last, or the list itself when none is left

Shift+F10.reason: the APG opens a tab's popup menu with it, and no menu exists until wave 5. A key bound to nothing is worse than a key a reader has to discover once.

deselectable.reason: Ark UI alone ships it. A tabs family holding no selection shows no panel, and content that closes entirely is what collapsible and accordion are for.

panelTransition.reason: Angular Material alone ships a sliding panel. It needs a clipping viewport that traps horizontal scrolling and fights the list's own scroll; the panel fades instead, which is what says it changed.

toolbarWrapper.reason: the row beside the list is a toolbar the consumer places in the actions part, not a second keyboard model inside this family.

trackless.reason: A set of tabs sitting on a card header's edge, a table's own rule or a panel that already draws its top border has a line the family cannot see. Two hairlines a pixel apart read as one smudge, and the only answer the field offers is Cloudscape's whole `container` variant — a second family's worth of paint to remove one line. With no track the marker sits on the item's own edge, so it lands on the line the page already drew.
